```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

How does uncertainty about demand change a merger analysis? This guide estimates
one PNB deposit-market model, checks the posterior, and compares policies using
the same recovered demand states. A final optional section compares four conduct
models. Read the [supplied-state starter](pnb-merger.html) ([source](https://github.com/luciu5/antitrustBayes/blob/main/vignettes/pnb-merger.Rmd)) first; it requires none
of this inference.

The estimation example uses `antitrustBayes` 0.3.0.9002's specification-15
relative Gaussian model, with `antitrust >= 0.99.43.9000`,
`coordination >= 0.1.0` and `cmdstanr >= 0.9.0`. Running it additionally requires
CmdStan and a C++ toolchain; see the
[setup instructions](https://github.com/luciu5/antitrustBayes#installation).
HMC and bridge sampling can take substantial time. **They are not executed when
this guide is built.** Posterior-dependent chunks are also unevaluated because
the build has no estimated `fit`. To run the example, execute its chunks in order
after setup. No estimated numerical output is supplied here.

## Set up one deposit-market question

This guide is self-contained. Prices are percent deposit rates, quantities are
thousands of dollars, and positive markdown ratios describe banks buying funds.
Lower rates harm depositors. The explicit candidate prior gives Bertrand,
Cournot and monopolistic competition .30 each, and auction conduct .10.

```{r data-and-priors}
library(antitrustBayes)
data(pnb)
owner_post <- pnb$group
owner_post[owner_post == attr(pnb, "target")] <- attr(pnb, "acquirer")
merger <- antitrust::counterfactual(ownership = owner_post)
supply_models <- c("bertrand", "cournot", "auction", "monopolistic")
model_priors <- bank_model_priors(supply_models)
model_priors
```

## Estimate Bertrand first

The local helper keeps observations, continuous priors and controls consistent
if you later estimate the other candidates. This call runs HMC with the default
CmdStanR backend. Current defaults are joint Gaussian share/margin errors,
collapsed market-specific persistent quality and active cross-equation
correlation where identified. The baseline proper-prior manifest is prespecified;
`?bayes_prior_manifest` describes sensitivity choices.

```{r estimate, eval=FALSE}
estimate_model <- function(sm) {
  bayes_est(
    prices = pnb$prices, quantities = pnb$quantities, margins = pnb$margins,
    market = rep("PHL", nrow(pnb)), group = pnb$group,
    demand_model = "logit", market_side = "input", supply_model = sm,
    share_basis = "relative", share_residual_model = "demand_shock",
    prior_manifest = "baseline", model_prior = model_priors[[sm]],
    stan_options = list(chains = 4, iter = 2000, warmup = 1000,
      cores = 4, seed = 1960,
      control = list(adapt_delta = .95, max_treedepth = 15))
  )
}
fit <- estimate_model("bertrand")
```

## Check inference before using policy tails

For this live CmdStanR fit, inspect both parameter and sampler diagnostics:

```{r diagnostics, eval=FALSE}
summary(fit)
fit@stanfit$diagnostic_summary()
```

Inspect R-hat, bulk and tail effective sample sizes, divergences, maximum-depth
hits and energy/BFMI diagnostics, with traces for parameters important to the
question. Investigate divergences rather than accepting them because they are a
small fraction of draws. Good mixing is not proof of identification or correct
institutional assumptions. Optional Nutpie and reloaded-fit extraction have
backend-specific contracts; see `?bayes_est` and `?"BayesFit-class"`.

## Reuse one posterior policy plan

New relative Gaussian fits separate persistent quality, period demand shocks and
independent measurement error. Recover quality and period demand jointly, then
retain them through both equilibria. Measurement noise remains in the observation
model. Its SD has a configurable Lognormal prior with median .10 and log SD .5;
the demand/measurement variance split can remain prior-dependent, especially in
a snapshot. The [model reference](supply-and-demand.html) ([source](https://github.com/luciu5/antitrustBayes/blob/main/vignettes/supply-and-demand.Rmd)) explains this state.

```{r paired-policies, eval=FALSE}
plan <- posterior_policy_draws(fit, n_draws = 200L, seed = 701)
posterior_merger <- simulate(fit, merger, draw_plan = plan, mc.cores = 1L)
observed_merger <- simulate(fit, merger, draw_plan = plan,
                            demand_anchoring = "observed", mc.cores = 1L)
calcPriceDelta(posterior_merger, market = TRUE, index = "paasche")
calcPriceDelta(observed_merger, market = TRUE, index = "paasche")
```

The first simulation uses the default `demand_anchoring = "latent_quality"`.
The plan aligns parameter draws, recovered quality and period demand,
outside-share normalization and role states where active. Its reconstructed
pre-policy rates and shares generally differ from observations. Each effect is
measured against that draw's **own pre-policy equilibrium**.

Explicit `"observed"` retains the historical observed-share calibration. This
paired comparison holds inference, priors, model probabilities and the existing
cost/value-of-funds recovery convention fixed. It changes anchoring, not the
likelihood or posterior. A supplied-state fit instead retains its supplied
calibration route; it has no estimated quality posterior.

Compatible specification-14 fits keep their original model interpretation.
Estimating specification 15 requires new inference and evidence before adopting
new model probabilities. `share_residual_model = "combined"` explicitly selects
the original residual model for a new fit; it does not convert saved fits.

## Define a harm quantity before a decision

Use the draw-wise Paasche index, which weights post-policy quantities within
each realization. It is not an equal-bank average, nor a weighted average of
bank-specific percentage changes. Report unavailable index draws before using
a posterior threshold probability:

```{r decision, eval=FALSE}
index_draws <- calcPriceDelta(posterior_merger, market = TRUE,
                              index = "paasche", posterior = TRUE)
c(requested = attr(index_draws, "n_draws"),
  valid = attr(index_draws, "n_valid"))
table(attr(index_draws, "failure_reason"), useNA = "no")
if (any(!is.finite(index_draws))) {
  stop("Decision withheld: inspect failed index draws before conditioning.")
}
merger_decision(-as.numeric(index_draws), threshold = .01,
                false_positive_cost = 1, false_negative_cost = 2)
```

The minus sign turns a deposit-rate reduction into positive harm. The threshold
is a **1% relative rate reduction**, not one percentage point. The decision
reports the probability of exceeding it and a challenge/clear action under the
stated loss ratio. The worked calculation withholds the decision if index draws
are unavailable. Conditioning on valid draws needs a separate, disclosed
analytical choice; do not silently discard failed banks or draws.

For an optional hypothetical-monopsonist calculation, pass the signed input-rate
threshold explicitly:

```{r input-hmt, eval=FALSE}
party_idx <- which(pnb$group %in%
                    c(attr(pnb, "acquirer"), attr(pnb, "target")))
hmt_draws <- HypoMonTest(posterior_merger, prodIndex = party_idx,
                         ssnip = -.05, posterior = TRUE)
requested <- attr(index_draws, "n_draws")
c(requested = requested, returned = length(hmt_draws),
  valid = sum(!is.na(hmt_draws)))
if (length(hmt_draws) != requested || anyNA(hmt_draws)) {
  stop("HMT summary withheld: inspect missing or failed HMT calculations.")
}
mean(hmt_draws)
```

This uses a 5% rate-reduction threshold. Its reported frequency includes every
requested calculation only after the length and missingness checks pass; HMT
solver failures are separate from price-index failures. A positive output-price SSNIP has the
wrong direction for depositors. See `?HypoMonTest` for the guideline convention
and `?"BayesSim-methods"` for other metrics and their scales.

## Optional: compare the complete conduct candidate set

You already have a one-model policy analysis. This extension estimates the other
three models and computes normalized bridge evidence; it runs no estimation or
evidence during documentation builds. Justify the candidate set by the trading
institution: bargaining is available in the API but excluded from this banking
baseline. Retain the same outcomes, market side, masks, share basis and
continuous-prior contracts across candidates.

```{r comparison, eval=FALSE}
fits <- setNames(lapply(supply_models, function(sm) {
  if (sm == "bertrand") fit else estimate_model(sm)
}), supply_models)
comp <- bayes_compare(
  bertrand = fits$bertrand, cournot = fits$cournot,
  auction = fits$auction, monopolistic = fits$monopolistic,
  prior_weights = model_priors
)
w <- bayes_weights(comp, "bridge")
```

Default collapsed-quality fits do **not** supply LOO/WAIC or stacking weights.
Bridge evidence is the demonstrated route; switching to sampled quality or a
different likelihood just to obtain an old scoring example would change the
analysis. Supported predictive-scoring units are described in `?bayes_compare`;
one market does not create meaningful held-out market clusters by naming them.

Every positive-prior candidate needs finite evidence before model probabilities
exist. Do not renormalize surviving candidates or substitute stacking when a
bridge calculation fails. Finite evidence alone does not establish numerical
accuracy: inspect bridge repetitions/uncertainty and each sampler's diagnostics.

```{r model-average, eval=FALSE}
plans <- lapply(fits, posterior_policy_draws, n_draws = 200L, seed = 701)
plans$bertrand <- plan
sims <- Map(function(f, p) simulate(f, merger, draw_plan = p, mc.cores = 1L),
            fits, plans)
set.seed(702)
avg <- bayes_avg(sims[names(w)], weights = w, n_draws = 1000L)
calcPriceDelta(avg, market = TRUE, index = "paasche")
sapply(avg@metadata$source_attrition,
       function(a) c(requested = a$requested, eligible = a$common_eligible))
```

The pooled valid count does not erase failures in source models. Inspect the
requested/eligible source counts and warnings: averaging can condition on
eligible draws within models while retaining the original mixture weights. A
positive-weight model with no eligible draw is an error. `?bayes_avg` documents
that distinction. Posterior dispersion describes economic uncertainty;
Monte Carlo error describes finite computation. Neither substitutes for checking
model assumptions and identification.
